title.suggested: Tom Allen's widow seeks to break his will

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen's widow in England would contest his will, which left $10 to each daughter and the rest to his nurse Tillie Hartgrove, claiming undue influence. The estate was worth $279.80.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, July 29, 1903', page 14.

facts.fact: Allen's will, drawn during his last illness, left $10 each to his daughters Polly Taylor of St. Louis and Mrs. J. H. Newey of Birmingham, England, and the rest to his housekeeper and nurse Tillie Hartgrove
Allen's widow, living in England, hired St. Louis attorney F. H. Sullivan to contest the will and claim a dower interest, arguing Allen was not of disposing mind and was unduly influenced
Allen had never divorced his wife in England, although they had not lived together for several years
Public Administrator Strode's appraisal of Allen's estate, filed July 28, valued it at $279.80

notes: The current summary says the widow 'contested' the will; the article says she intends to contest it. The will's $10 bequests went to the daughters here, not to sisters as in the index entry (id 000). This conflicts with the Post-Dispatch of the day before (1011), which says the will left everything to the two daughters.
